title: John, in 21 days
blurb: One chapter a day through the gospel written so that you would believe. The best first plan for anyone who has never read a book of the Bible through.

days.note: The Word became flesh. The claim is made before the story starts.
Water into wine, and the temple cleared. Both are signs, not errands.
Nicodemus comes at night, and gets told he must start again.
A Samaritan woman is given the plainest answer anyone in this book gets.
A healing on the Sabbath, and the argument that will end in a cross.
Bread for five thousand, then a sermon that empties the room.
Even his own brothers do not believe him.
“Before Abraham came into existence, I AM.” They pick up stones.
A blind man sees. The people who can see do not.
The shepherd who owns the sheep, and lays down his life for them.
Lazarus. Note that Jesus weeps knowing exactly what he is about to do.
The last public week. A jar of perfume is broken and criticised.
He washes their feet — including the feet of the man leaving to betray him.
“I am the way.” Comfort spoken to men hours from losing everything.
The vine. Fruit is the result of remaining, not of straining.
The Spirit promised, and sorrow told plainly that it will turn.
Jesus prays for those who will believe through their word. That is you.
The arrest, and Peter warming himself at the wrong fire.
The crucifixion. “It is finished.”
The empty tomb — and Thomas allowed his doubt without being shamed.
Breakfast on a beach. Peter is restored three times, once for each denial.

title: Psalms for a hard season
blurb: Fourteen psalms for grief, fear, exhaustion and doubt — including the one that does not resolve. Nothing here asks you to feel better than you do.

days.note: Thirst, and a man arguing with his own soul.
“How long?” Four times. The Bible permits this.
Read it as an adult, not as a memory from school.
Confidence and terror in the same poem.
Written by a man who had just escaped by pretending to be mad.
He waited patiently — the waiting is in the text.
Be still. The verse is set in an earthquake, not a quiet room.
David after the worst thing he ever did.
For God alone my soul waits in silence.
The prosperity of the wicked, faced honestly and then reframed.
The psalm with no happy ending. It is in the Bible on purpose.
Bless the Lord — a deliberate act of remembering.
A travelling song for anyone a long way from home.
Known completely, and still held.

title: Mark, in 16 days
blurb: The fastest of the four gospels, written for people with no religious background and no patience. A fortnight, and you have read a life of Jesus.

days.note: Everything at speed. “Immediately” is this book's pulse.
Four friends dig through a roof rather than wait their turn.
His family come to take him home, believing he is out of his mind.
Parables about soil, and a storm told to be quiet.
A legion, a bleeding woman, and a dead girl — all in one chapter.
John the Baptist is executed. Five thousand are fed.
Tradition against commandment, and a foreign woman who argues and wins.
The hinge of the book: “But who do you say that I am?”
The transfiguration, and the most honest prayer in Scripture.
The rich man walks away. A blind beggar refuses to be quiet.
Into Jerusalem. The fig tree and the temple are the same judgement.
The greatest commandment, and a widow who gives everything.
The temple will fall. Watch.
The anointing, the supper, Gethsemane, the arrest. Read it slowly.
Trial, crucifixion, and the verdict of a Roman soldier.
The tomb is empty, and the oldest ending stops mid-sentence.
